lens: Prospective applicant; keyboard-oriented use (simulated AI lens)
reason: The reviewed source supports a coherent applicant journey: the public proposition identifies student-led consulting, Join explains eligibility, preparation and evaluation, and the application separates draft saving from submission. Native fields, explicit validation focus, step-heading focus, and recovery comparisons are promising for keyboard use. Browser and server conflicts pause writes until an explicit choice; the review step explains consent and the submission transition. Applicant next-action logic distinguishes scheduling outages from having nothing to do. Desktop-hero and mobile captures show a consistent Precision Instrument identity, readable hierarchy and clear student entry points, but do not show private applicant screens. Original-resume access is accurately disclosed in Materials and Review; pending client proof is labeled without invented outcomes. Supplied local tests and the database race log support specific reliability claims. They do not establish a complete keyboard-only journey, hosted integration, or observed student success, so an unqualified world-class or release endorsement is not established.
inspected: src/app/applicant/page.tsx (dashboard loading, next-action selection and receipt)
tests/e2e/application-reliability.spec.ts (navigation, storage failure, submission lock, recovery and conflict cases)

findings.evidence: The interrupted-submit journey at lines 8–42 advances with click/check and replaces /applicant with a synthetic Submitted heading. Recovery cases beginning at lines 155 and 231 assert heading focus but choose copies with click. public-journeys.spec.ts:13–27 checks Escape focus return after programmatic focus; its preparation journey at lines 30–37 uses clicks. These checks do not demonstrate sequential keyboard access through preparation, file selection, conflict choice, consent, submission and the real next-action surface.
findings.userImpact: A keyboard-dependent applicant has only partial evidence that they can complete the full task and locate the next action after recovery or submission; no actual keyboard failure is claimed.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a focused keyboard-only applicant acceptance scenario using Tab/Shift+Tab, Enter/Space and native select keys, asserting visible focus and focus return across validation, both conflict choices and submission. Include the real applicant status rendering; separately record authenticated integration validation when an environment exists.

notVerified: No live browser or new tests were run by this seat; the journey was traced through source and supplied synthetic test evidence, not observed with a student.
No staging or hosted Clerk signup/session-expiry, Supabase RPC/RLS, storage upload or email-delivery acceptance exists in this package.
Private application/recovery/status visual craft, long keyboard traversal and focus visibility at zoom were not demonstrated by supplied captures.
Physical devices, Safari, Firefox, screen readers and actual applicant understanding of saved/submitted state remain unverified.
Migration/application rollout coordination, Board privacy policy resolution and client publication approvals remain external dependencies.
